prompt: Which of the following best defines a government budget deficit?

options.label: A
options.text: Government purchases equal transfer payments while tax revenues remain unchanged

options.label: B
options.text: Government purchases plus transfer payments exceed tax revenues during a given year

options.label: C
options.text: Interest payments on accumulated debt exceed government purchases during a given year

options.label: D
options.text: Tax revenues exceed government purchases plus transfer payments during a given year

options.label: E
options.text: The national debt is larger at the end of the year than the country's annual tax revenue

explanation: A budget deficit occurs when annual government purchases plus transfer payments exceed annual tax revenues. The shortfall must be financed, so a deficit is an annual flow rather than the accumulated debt stock.

prompt: Which of the following best defines a government budget surplus?

options.label: A
options.text: Tax revenues equal government purchases while transfer payments are positive

options.label: B
options.text: The national debt exceeds the government's annual tax revenues at the end of the year

options.label: C
options.text: Government purchases plus transfer payments exceed tax revenues during a given year

options.label: D
options.text: Tax revenues exceed government purchases plus transfer payments during a given year

options.label: E
options.text: Interest payments on accumulated debt are smaller than total transfer payments

explanation: A budget surplus occurs when annual tax revenues exceed government purchases plus transfer payments.

prompt: The national debt is best described as

options.label: A
options.text: The amount by which government outlays exceed tax revenues in one particular year

options.label: B
options.text: The annual interest payment the government makes on outstanding obligations

options.label: C
options.text: The annual total of government purchases and transfer payments combined

options.label: D
options.text: The accumulated amount the government owes as a result of past borrowing

options.label: E
options.text: The amount of tax revenue collected but not spent during the current year

explanation: The national debt is the accumulated stock of government borrowing from past periods.

prompt: If a government runs a budget deficit in a given year, which of the following will most likely occur?

options.label: A
options.text: The national debt will increase because the government must finance the shortfall

options.label: B
options.text: The budget will automatically become a surplus because outstanding debt is positive

options.label: C
options.text: The annual deficit will become part of tax revenue in the following fiscal year

options.label: D
options.text: The national debt will be eliminated once the annual budget moves into deficit

options.label: E
options.text: The national debt will decrease because tax revenues are less than government outlays

explanation: A deficit means current outlays exceed current tax revenues, so the government must finance the gap.

prompt: Which expression correctly represents the government budget surplus?

options.label: A
options.text: Transfer payments − (government purchases + tax revenues)

options.label: B
options.text: Government purchases − (tax revenues + transfer payments)

options.label: C
options.text: Government purchases + transfer payments − tax revenues

options.label: D
options.text: Tax revenues + government purchases − transfer payments

options.label: E
options.text: Tax revenues − (government purchases + transfer payments)

explanation: The budget surplus equals tax revenues minus the sum of government purchases and transfer payments.

prompt: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a budget deficit from the national debt?

options.label: A
options.text: A deficit is an accumulated stock, while the national debt is an annual flow

options.label: B
options.text: Both are accumulated stocks, but a deficit includes only transfer payments

options.label: C
options.text: A deficit is an annual flow, while the national debt is an accumulated stock

options.label: D
options.text: Both are annual flows, but the national debt includes only interest payments

options.label: E
options.text: A deficit measures tax revenue, while the national debt measures government purchases

explanation: A deficit or surplus is measured over a period, so it is a flow.

prompt: Why can a larger national debt impose a greater burden on a government?

options.label: A
options.text: A larger debt automatically raises tax revenues enough to cover all additional interest payments

options.label: B
options.text: A larger debt prevents the government from making any purchases until the debt is completely repaid

options.label: C
options.text: A larger debt converts annual budget deficits into surpluses without any change in fiscal choices

options.label: D
options.text: A larger debt eliminates transfer payments because debt service replaces all other government outlays

options.label: E
options.text: A larger debt can require greater interest payments, leaving fewer funds for alternative uses

explanation: Interest must be paid on accumulated government debt.

prompt: The opportunity cost of using government revenue to make interest payments on the national debt is

options.label: A
options.text: The amount of national debt that remains outstanding after the interest is paid

options.label: B
options.text: The alternative government purchases or transfers that those funds could otherwise support

options.label: C
options.text: The annual budget surplus that necessarily results whenever interest payments are made

options.label: D
options.text: The previous budget deficits that originally caused the national debt to accumulate

options.label: E
options.text: The tax revenues that were collected in earlier years before the debt was issued

explanation: The opportunity cost of debt service is what the government gives up by using scarce revenue for interest payments. Those same funds could have supported alternative purchases, transfers, or other public priorities.

prompt: Assume tax revenues exactly equal government purchases plus transfer payments. Which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The government has a balanced budget for that year

options.label: B
options.text: The government has a budget surplus equal to its government purchases

options.label: C
options.text: The national debt must equal zero at the end of that year

options.label: D
options.text: The national debt must fall by the amount of annual tax revenue

options.label: E
options.text: The government has a budget deficit equal to its transfer payments

explanation: When tax revenues exactly equal government purchases plus transfers, the annual budget balance is zero. A balanced current budget does not imply that previously accumulated national debt is zero.

prompt: When calculating the annual government budget balance in Topic 5.4, transfer payments are

options.label: A
options.text: Added to tax revenues because transfers are received by households rather than firms

options.label: B
options.text: Included with government purchases as government outlays compared with tax revenues

options.label: C
options.text: Excluded because only government purchases affect the annual government budget balance

options.label: D
options.text: Counted as reductions in the national debt regardless of the annual budget position

options.label: E
options.text: Subtracted from government purchases before the result is compared with tax revenues

explanation: For the Topic 5.4 budget balance, total government outlays include both purchases and transfer payments.

prompt: A government collects $900 billion in taxes, purchases $750 billion of goods and services, and makes $100 billion in transfer payments. What is its budget balance?

options.label: A
options.text: A balanced budget

options.label: B
options.text: A $50 billion surplus

options.label: C
options.text: A $50 billion deficit

options.label: D
options.text: A $250 billion deficit

options.label: E
options.text: A $150 billion surplus

explanation: Budget balance = 900 - (750 + 100) = +50 billion.

prompt: A government collects $820 billion in taxes, makes $780 billion in purchases, and pays $90 billion in transfers. What is its budget balance?

options.label: A
options.text: A $50 billion deficit

options.label: B
options.text: A balanced budget

options.label: C
options.text: A $40 billion surplus

options.label: D
options.text: A $90 billion deficit

options.label: E
options.text: A $50 billion surplus

explanation: Budget balance = 820 - (780 + 90) = -50 billion.

prompt: Tax revenues are $1.20 trillion, government purchases are $1.05 trillion, and transfer payments are $0.20 trillion. Which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The government has a balanced budget

options.label: B
options.text: The government runs a $0.25 trillion surplus

options.label: C
options.text: The government runs a $0.05 trillion deficit

options.label: D
options.text: The government runs a $0.15 trillion deficit

options.label: E
options.text: The government runs a $0.05 trillion surplus

explanation: Budget balance = 1.20 - (1.05 + 0.20) = -0.05 trillion.

prompt: Government purchases are $640 billion and transfer payments are $160 billion. What level of tax revenue would produce a balanced budget?

options.label: A
options.text: $720 billion

options.label: B
options.text: $640 billion

options.label: C
options.text: $960 billion

options.label: D
options.text: $800 billion

options.label: E
options.text: $480 billion

explanation: A balanced budget requires tax revenue to equal purchases plus transfers.

prompt: Government purchases plus transfer payments total $600 billion, while tax revenues are $560 billion. The government has

options.label: A
options.text: A $160 billion budget surplus

options.label: B
options.text: A $40 billion budget surplus

options.label: C
options.text: A balanced budget

options.label: D
options.text: A $160 billion budget deficit

options.label: E
options.text: A $40 billion budget deficit

explanation: Total outlays exceed tax revenues by 600 - 560 = 40 billion.

prompt: Total government purchases and transfer payments are $700 billion. What tax revenue would produce a $30 billion budget surplus?

options.label: A
options.text: $670 billion

options.label: B
options.text: $770 billion

options.label: C
options.text: $730 billion

options.label: D
options.text: $700 billion

options.label: E
options.text: $760 billion

explanation: A $30 billion surplus requires taxes to exceed total outlays by $30 billion.

prompt: Tax revenues are $500 billion and government purchases are $460 billion. What level of transfer payments would result in a $20 billion budget deficit?

options.label: A
options.text: $40 billion

options.label: B
options.text: $80 billion

options.label: C
options.text: $100 billion

options.label: D
options.text: $20 billion

options.label: E
options.text: $60 billion

explanation: For a $20 billion deficit, purchases plus transfers must equal $520 billion when taxes are $500 billion.

prompt: Tax revenues are $900 billion and transfer payments are $200 billion. What level of government purchases would produce a balanced budget?

options.label: A
options.text: $800 billion

options.label: B
options.text: $900 billion

options.label: C
options.text: $1.1 trillion

options.label: D
options.text: $700 billion

options.label: E
options.text: $600 billion

explanation: A balanced budget requires purchases + transfers = tax revenue.

prompt: Country A collects $600 billion in taxes and has $650 billion in total government purchases and transfers. Country B collects $800 billion in taxes and has $820 billion in total government purchases and transfers. Which country has the larger budget deficit?

options.label: A
options.text: Country A, by $30 billion

options.label: B
options.text: Country B, by $30 billion

options.label: C
options.text: Country A, by $50 billion

options.label: D
options.text: Country B, by $20 billion

options.label: E
options.text: Both have the same budget deficit

explanation: Country A has a $50 billion deficit, while Country B has a $20 billion deficit.

prompt: Tax revenues increase by $40 billion while government purchases and transfer payments do not change. If the government initially had a deficit, the deficit will

options.label: A
options.text: Decrease by the amount of existing debt

options.label: B
options.text: Become a surplus of exactly $40 billion

options.label: C
options.text: Increase by $40 billion

options.label: D
options.text: Remain unchanged because purchases did not change

options.label: E
options.text: Decrease by $40 billion

explanation: Higher tax revenue improves the budget balance dollar for dollar when outlays are unchanged.

prompt: A government begins the year with $2.0 trillion in national debt and runs a $100 billion budget deficit. Ignoring other changes, what is the debt at year-end?

options.label: A
options.text: $2.1 trillion

options.label: B
options.text: $2.2 trillion

options.label: C
options.text: $2.0 trillion

options.label: D
options.text: $2.5 trillion

options.label: E
options.text: $1.9 trillion

explanation: A budget deficit adds to outstanding debt.

prompt: A government begins the year with $5 trillion in national debt and has a balanced budget for the year. Ignoring other changes, the national debt will

options.label: A
options.text: Fall to zero

options.label: B
options.text: Fall by the amount of government purchases

options.label: C
options.text: Rise by the amount of transfer payments

options.label: D
options.text: Remain at $5 trillion

options.label: E
options.text: Rise by the amount of tax revenue

explanation: With a balanced annual budget, there is no current-year deficit to add to debt and no surplus specified to retire it. Under the stated assumptions, the debt remains $5 trillion.

prompt: A government begins the year with $3.0 trillion in debt and runs a $50 billion budget surplus that is used to retire outstanding debt. What is the year-end debt?

options.label: A
options.text: $3.50 trillion

options.label: B
options.text: $3.00 trillion

options.label: C
options.text: $2.95 trillion

options.label: D
options.text: $3.05 trillion

options.label: E
options.text: $2.50 trillion

explanation: A surplus used to retire debt reduces the accumulated stock.

prompt: A government starts with $1.5 trillion in national debt and then runs deficits of $80 billion and $120 billion in two successive years. Ignoring other changes, the debt after the second year is

options.label: A
options.text: $1.30 trillion

options.label: B
options.text: $1.50 trillion

options.label: C
options.text: $1.70 trillion

options.label: D
options.text: $1.90 trillion

options.label: E
options.text: $1.62 trillion

explanation: The two deficits add $200 billion in total to the existing debt.

prompt: Which annual budget outcome directly adds to the national debt?

options.label: A
options.text: A budget surplus

options.label: B
options.text: A budget deficit

options.label: C
options.text: A reduction in transfer payments that creates a surplus

options.label: D
options.text: Tax revenues equal to total outlays

options.label: E
options.text: A balanced budget

explanation: A deficit is the annual budget outcome that requires financing and therefore adds to the national debt. A balanced budget adds no new deficit, while a surplus can be used to reduce debt.

prompt: A government has $4 trillion in national debt and pays an average annual interest rate of 3 percent. Approximately how much interest must it pay in one year?

options.label: A
options.text: $12 billion

options.label: B
options.text: $40 billion

options.label: C
options.text: $1.2 trillion

options.label: D
options.text: $120 billion

options.label: E
options.text: $300 billion

explanation: Annual interest is 3% of $4 trillion, or $0.12 trillion.

prompt: A government has $6 trillion in national debt and pays an average annual interest rate of 5 percent. Its annual interest payment is approximately

options.label: A
options.text: $500 billion

options.label: B
options.text: $300 billion

options.label: C
options.text: $30 billion

options.label: D
options.text: $1.2 trillion

options.label: E
options.text: $120 billion

explanation: Annual interest is 5% of $6 trillion, which equals $0.30 trillion or $300 billion.

prompt: If the national debt rises while the average interest rate on that debt remains unchanged, annual interest payments will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Become part of tax revenue rather than an obligation of the government

options.label: B
options.text: Remain unchanged because the interest rate, not the debt level, determines interest payments

options.label: C
options.text: Decrease because larger debt lowers the government's annual financing needs

options.label: D
options.text: Fall to zero once the government begins running annual budget deficits

options.label: E
options.text: Increase because interest is paid on a larger amount of debt

explanation: With the interest rate unchanged, a larger debt principal produces a larger interest payment.

prompt: If a larger share of government revenue must be used to pay interest on accumulated debt, which of the following is most directly affected?

options.label: A
options.text: The accounting identity used to classify a balanced budget

options.label: B
options.text: The definition of the annual budget deficit

options.label: C
options.text: The amount of revenue available for alternative government uses

options.label: D
options.text: The distinction between tax revenues and transfer payments

options.label: E
options.text: The fact that a deficit is an annual flow

explanation: Revenue committed to interest cannot simultaneously be used for other government purposes.

prompt: A government cannot cover a required interest payment from current revenues and finances the payment by additional borrowing. Which of the following will most likely occur?

options.label: A
options.text: The national debt will increase further

options.label: B
options.text: Tax revenues will rise by exactly the interest payment

options.label: C
options.text: The national debt will fall by the interest payment

options.label: D
options.text: The annual budget will automatically become balanced

options.label: E
options.text: The existing debt will be converted into a budget surplus

explanation: If interest is financed with new borrowing, the government issues additional debt to make the payment.

prompt: Tax revenues rise by $20 billion, government purchases rise by $50 billion, and transfer payments fall by $10 billion. What happens to the government budget balance?

options.label: A
options.text: It improves by $20 billion

options.label: B
options.text: It improves by $40 billion

options.label: C
options.text: It is unchanged

options.label: D
options.text: It worsens by $40 billion

options.label: E
options.text: It worsens by $20 billion

explanation: The change in the budget balance is +20 - 50 + 10 = -20 billion, because lower transfers improve the balance. The budget therefore worsens by $20 billion.

prompt: Tax revenues fall by $30 billion, government purchases fall by $10 billion, and transfer payments rise by $15 billion. The budget balance will

options.label: A
options.text: Worsen by $35 billion

options.label: B
options.text: Worsen by $15 billion

options.label: C
options.text: Improve by $35 billion

options.label: D
options.text: Improve by $5 billion

options.label: E
options.text: Remain unchanged

explanation: The change is -30 + 10 - 15 = -35 billion: lower taxes and higher transfers worsen the balance, while lower purchases partly offset them. The net effect is a $35 billion deterioration.

prompt: Government purchases fall by $40 billion while transfer payments rise by $20 billion and tax revenues are unchanged. The budget balance will

options.label: A
options.text: Remain unchanged

options.label: B
options.text: Improve by $20 billion

options.label: C
options.text: Worsen by $20 billion

options.label: D
options.text: Improve by $60 billion

options.label: E
options.text: Worsen by $60 billion

explanation: A $40 billion decline in purchases improves the balance, while a $20 billion rise in transfers worsens it.

prompt: Two governments each have $2 trillion in national debt. Government X pays an average interest rate of 3 percent and Government Y pays 5 percent. Which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.text: Government Y must have a smaller national debt because its interest rate is higher

options.label: B
options.text: Both governments have the same annual interest burden because their debt levels are equal

options.label: C
options.text: Government Y has the larger annual interest burden

options.label: D
options.text: Government X must have a larger annual deficit because its interest rate is lower

options.label: E
options.text: Government X has the larger annual interest burden

explanation: With equal debt stocks, the government paying the higher average interest rate owes more interest each year. At 5 percent versus 3 percent, Government Y has the larger debt-service burden.

prompt: Two governments make the same annual interest payment, but Government A has a smaller national debt than Government B. Which conclusion is most consistent with the information?

options.label: A
options.text: Government B must collect less tax revenue than Government A

options.label: B
options.text: Government B must have larger transfer payments than Government A

options.label: C
options.text: Government A must have a larger budget deficit than Government B

options.label: D
options.text: Government A must be paying a higher average interest rate on its debt

options.label: E
options.text: Both governments must have identical annual budget balances

explanation: Interest payment equals debt times the average interest rate. If A has less debt but makes the same payment as B, A must have the higher average rate.

prompt: A government has fixed tax revenue for the year. If required interest payments on its accumulated debt rise, which of the following best describes the burden identified in Topic 5.4?

options.label: A
options.text: More of the existing revenue must be devoted to debt service rather than alternative uses

options.label: B
options.text: The government automatically acquires a budget surplus because debt service has increased

options.label: C
options.text: The budget deficit is redefined as tax revenue minus interest payments only

options.label: D
options.text: The national debt becomes an annual flow instead of an accumulated stock

options.label: E
options.text: Transfer payments are no longer included when determining the annual budget balance

explanation: Higher required interest payments absorb a larger share of a fixed revenue pool. That leaves fewer funds available for alternative government uses, which is the burden emphasized by POL-3.B.3.

prompt: Which of the following pairs correctly identifies a flow variable and a stock variable?

options.label: A
options.text: National debt: flow; annual interest payment: stock

options.label: B
options.text: Budget deficit: flow; national debt: stock

options.label: C
options.text: Tax revenue: stock; budget deficit: stock

options.label: D
options.text: Budget deficit: stock; national debt: flow

options.label: E
options.text: Budget surplus: stock; national debt: flow

explanation: A budget deficit is measured for a particular period and is therefore a flow. National debt is the accumulated amount owed at a point in time and is therefore a stock.

prompt: A government has a balanced budget this year but begins the year with substantial national debt. Which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The national debt becomes equal to current-year government purchases

options.label: B
options.text: The balanced budget does not by itself eliminate the previously accumulated debt

options.label: C
options.text: The government must have a surplus because positive national debt cannot coexist with a balanced budget

options.label: D
options.text: The government must have a deficit equal to the interest owed on its existing debt

options.label: E
options.text: The national debt must fall to zero because current tax revenue equals current outlays

explanation: A balanced current budget means no new annual shortfall, not that past borrowing disappears. Existing national debt can remain even when the current year is balanced.

prompt: Which of the following can occur when a government already has a large national debt?

options.label: A
options.text: It must run a surplus because any positive debt automatically raises tax revenue

options.label: B
options.text: It must run a deficit because outstanding debt prevents a current-year surplus

options.label: C
options.text: It must have a balanced budget because debt measures only past fiscal outcomes

options.label: D
options.text: It can still run either a deficit, a surplus, or a balanced budget in the current year

options.label: E
options.text: It cannot make transfer payments until the accumulated debt is fully repaid

explanation: The existing debt stock does not determine the sign of the current-year budget balance. Current taxes, purchases, and transfers can produce a deficit, surplus, or balance regardless of the inherited debt level.

prompt: A government records a budget surplus this year while national debt remains positive. Which of the following best explains this outcome?

options.label: A
options.text: The surplus is a current-year flow, while the debt reflects accumulated past borrowing

options.label: B
options.text: The national debt measures only current-year interest payments, not past borrowing

options.label: C
options.text: A budget surplus is counted as part of national debt, so both must remain positive

options.label: D
options.text: A government with positive debt is automatically classified as running a surplus

options.label: E
options.text: The surplus and debt are the same measure expressed over different units of time

explanation: A current-year surplus and a positive debt stock can coexist because they measure different things. The surplus is one year's flow, whereas debt reflects accumulated past borrowing.

prompt: A government begins with $1.0 trillion in national debt, runs deficits of $50 billion and $80 billion, and then runs a $20 billion surplus used to retire debt. Ignoring other changes, ending debt is

options.label: A
options.text: $1.15 trillion

options.label: B
options.text: $0.89 trillion

options.label: C
options.text: $1.11 trillion

options.label: D
options.text: $1.05 trillion

options.label: E
options.text: $1.13 trillion

explanation: Net debt change is +50 + 80 - 20 = +110 billion.

prompt: A government begins with $2.4 trillion in national debt, then runs a $100 billion surplus followed by deficits of $60 billion and $40 billion. If the surplus retires debt, ending debt is

options.label: A
options.text: $2.4 trillion

options.label: B
options.text: $2.6 trillion

options.label: C
options.text: $2.5 trillion

options.label: D
options.text: $2.3 trillion

options.label: E
options.text: $2.2 trillion

explanation: The $100 billion surplus reduces debt, while the later $60 billion and $40 billion deficits add exactly $100 billion back. Ending debt therefore returns to $2.4 trillion.

prompt: A government starts with $800 billion in debt and runs a $30 billion deficit in each of the next three years. Ignoring other changes, the debt after three years is

options.label: A
options.text: $830 billion

options.label: B
options.text: $920 billion

options.label: C
options.text: $890 billion

options.label: D
options.text: $710 billion

options.label: E
options.text: $860 billion

explanation: Three $30 billion deficits add $90 billion to the debt stock.

prompt: A government ends a two-year period with $1.46 trillion in debt after running deficits of $40 billion and $70 billion. What was its debt at the beginning of the period?

options.label: A
options.text: $1.27 trillion

options.label: B
options.text: $1.39 trillion

options.label: C
options.text: $1.57 trillion

options.label: D
options.text: $1.46 trillion

options.label: E
options.text: $1.35 trillion

explanation: The two deficits total $110 billion, so beginning debt must have been $1.46 trillion - $0.11 trillion = $1.35 trillion. The annual deficits explain the increase in the debt stock.

prompt: National debt increases from $3.20 trillion to $3.27 trillion during a year. If the increase is entirely due to the annual budget position, the government ran

options.label: A
options.text: A $70 billion surplus

options.label: B
options.text: A $270 billion deficit

options.label: C
options.text: A $70 billion deficit

options.label: D
options.text: A $7 billion deficit

options.label: E
options.text: A balanced budget

explanation: The debt stock rose by $70 billion.

prompt: Tax revenues are $760 billion, government purchases are $590 billion, and transfer payments rise from $140 billion to $190 billion. Holding everything else constant, the budget moves from

options.label: A
options.text: A $30 billion deficit to a $20 billion surplus

options.label: B
options.text: A balanced budget to a $50 billion deficit

options.label: C
options.text: A $170 billion surplus to a $120 billion surplus

options.label: D
options.text: A $20 billion surplus to a $30 billion deficit

options.label: E
options.text: A $30 billion surplus to a $20 billion deficit

explanation: Initially, the balance is 760 - (590 + 140) = +30 billion. After transfers rise to 190, the balance becomes 760 - 780 = -20 billion.

prompt: Tax revenues and transfer payments both increase by $25 billion while government purchases are unchanged. What happens to the budget balance?

options.label: A
options.text: It improves by $50 billion because tax revenues and transfers both rise

options.label: B
options.text: It worsens by $50 billion because both changes raise government outlays

options.label: C
options.text: It improves by $25 billion because only tax revenue affects the budget balance

options.label: D
options.text: It is unchanged because the two changes offset exactly

options.label: E
options.text: It worsens by $25 billion because only transfer payments affect the budget balance

explanation: A $25 billion tax increase improves the balance by $25 billion, while a $25 billion transfer increase worsens it by the same amount. The two effects exactly offset.

prompt: Government purchases and tax revenues both fall by $25 billion while transfer payments are unchanged. The budget balance will

options.label: A
options.text: Improve by $25 billion

options.label: B
options.text: Worsen by $50 billion

options.label: C
options.text: Improve by $50 billion

options.label: D
options.text: Remain unchanged

options.label: E
options.text: Worsen by $25 billion

explanation: Lower purchases improve the balance by $25 billion, but lower tax revenue worsens it by $25 billion. With transfers unchanged, the net budget effect is zero.

prompt: Tax revenues and transfer payments both rise by $15 billion, with government purchases unchanged. If the government initially had a $60 billion deficit, the new deficit is

options.label: A
options.text: $90 billion

options.label: B
options.text: $45 billion

options.label: C
options.text: $30 billion

options.label: D
options.text: $75 billion

options.label: E
options.text: $60 billion

explanation: Equal increases in taxes and transfers have opposite, equal effects on the budget balance.

prompt: Government purchases and tax revenues both rise by $40 billion, while transfer payments are unchanged. If the initial budget was balanced, the new budget will be

options.label: A
options.text: An $80 billion surplus

options.label: B
options.text: Balanced

options.label: C
options.text: An $80 billion deficit

options.label: D
options.text: A $40 billion deficit

options.label: E
options.text: A $40 billion surplus

prompt: A government has $2 trillion in debt. Its average interest rate rises from 4 percent to 5 percent. By how much does its annual interest payment increase?

prompt: A government collects $1.0 trillion in tax revenue and must devote $200 billion to interest on accumulated debt. Before considering other spending, how much of that tax revenue remains available for alternative uses?

prompt: Required interest payments rise by $50 billion and the government finances the entire increase through additional borrowing rather than reducing other outlays or raising taxes. What is the direct effect on the national debt?

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: E

explanation: Borrowing the full additional $50 billion interest cost increases the debt stock by that same amount. Financing debt service through new debt can therefore compound the fiscal burden.

prompt: Which of the following best illustrates the opportunity cost of debt-service payments?

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: Reducing national debt by $80 billion after running an annual surplus

options.label: D

options.label: E
options.text: Collecting $80 billion more in tax revenue than government outlays

explanation: Opportunity cost asks what is forgone when scarce resources are used for one purpose. Using $80 billion for interest means that same $80 billion cannot be used for other government priorities.

prompt: Which policy change would improve the government budget balance by the greatest amount, all else equal?

prompt: A government moves from a $100 billion deficit to a $40 billion deficit. Which of the following is true for the second year, assuming no other debt changes?

options.label: A

options.label: E

prompt: A government reduces its annual budget deficit from $80 billion to $20 billion. Ignoring other changes, national debt in the second year will

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: Increase by $80 billion

options.label: E
options.text: Decrease by $60 billion

explanation: A positive $20 billion deficit adds $20 billion to the accumulated debt. Reducing a deficit does not reduce debt unless the budget actually moves into surplus and that surplus retires debt.

prompt: A government moves from a $40 billion deficit to a $10 billion surplus that is used to retire debt. Compared with the previous year, which of the following occurs?

options.label: E

prompt: Which statement about a smaller budget deficit is correct?

options.label: A

prompt: The national debt can rise even while the annual deficit is falling if

prompt: Tax revenues fall by $30 billion at the same time government purchases fall by $20 billion and transfer payments fall by $10 billion. What happens to the budget balance?

prompt: A government collects $900 billion in taxes and has $900 billion in combined purchases and transfers. It also begins the year with $4 trillion in national debt. Which statement is correct?

prompt: A government initially has a $50 billion deficit. Tax revenues rise by $30 billion, government purchases rise by $10 billion, and transfer payments fall by $5 billion. What is the new budget position?

prompt: A government begins with $2.6 trillion in debt, runs a $100 billion deficit in year 1, and has a balanced budget in year 2. Ignoring other changes, debt at the end of year 2 is

prompt: Two governments have the same national debt and pay the same average interest rate, but one collects more tax revenue. Which of the following must be true about their annual interest payments?

prompt: A government has $1.2 trillion in debt and uses a $70 billion surplus to retire debt. If no other debt changes occur, the new debt level is

prompt: A government has tax revenues of $650 billion and total purchases plus transfers of $700 billion. It then reduces transfer payments by $30 billion with no other change. Which of the following is true?

prompt: Government A begins with $2.0 trillion in debt and runs deficits of $60 billion and $40 billion. Government B begins with $2.05 trillion in debt and runs deficits of $20 billion and $30 billion. Ignoring other changes, which government ends with more debt and by how much?

prompt: A government's annual interest payment rises by $40 billion while tax revenue is unchanged. Which conclusion can be made without knowing how other government outlays change?

prompt: A government begins with $2.2 trillion in national debt. Year 1 has a $70 billion deficit. In year 2, tax revenue is $950 billion, purchases are $760 billion, and transfers are $150 billion. What is national debt at the end of year 2, assuming any surplus is used to retire debt?

prompt: A government reduces its deficit from $150 billion to $40 billion. Which of the following statements is necessarily true, assuming no other changes to debt?

prompt: Assume the average interest rate on government debt is unchanged. Which sequence best explains why repeated deficits can create a growing fiscal burden?

prompt: A government has $4 trillion in debt at an average interest rate of 5 percent. It uses a $400 billion surplus to retire debt. If the interest rate remains 5 percent, next year's annual interest payment falls by

prompt: Two governments both end a two-year period with $1.2 trillion in debt. prompt: A government begins with $100 billion in debt and, with no other budget imbalance, finances annual interest at 10 percent entirely through new borrowing. What is the debt after two years?

prompt: Government A has $3 trillion in debt at 4 percent interest; Government B has $2 trillion in debt at 6 percent interest. Which statement is true?

prompt: Policy X produces deficits of $30 billion and $40 billion over two years. Policy Y produces a $10 billion surplus followed by a $90 billion deficit. Starting from the same debt, which policy leaves the larger debt after two years if the surplus retires debt?

options.label: A
options.text: Policy X, by $20 billion

options.label: B
options.text: Policy Y, by $20 billion

options.label: C
options.text: Policy X, by $10 billion

options.label: D
options.text: Policy Y, by $10 billion

options.label: E
options.text: Both leave the same debt

explanation: Policy X adds $70 billion net to debt. Policy Y changes debt by -10 + 90 = +80 billion, so Y leaves $10 billion more debt than X.

prompt: Government purchases are $620 billion and transfer payments are $180 billion. What tax revenue is required to prevent the national debt from increasing because of the current annual budget?

options.label: A
options.text: $440 billion

options.label: B
options.text: $800 billion

options.label: C
options.text: $980 billion

options.label: D
options.text: $1.0 trillion

options.label: E
options.text: $620 billion

explanation: Preventing a current-year deficit requires tax revenue to equal purchases plus transfers. Here, 620 + 180 = $800 billion.

prompt: A government wants to reduce outstanding debt by $60 billion this year and will use its entire budget surplus to retire debt. What annual budget balance is required?

options.label: A
options.text: A $120 billion surplus

options.label: B
options.text: A $30 billion surplus

options.label: C
options.text: A $60 billion deficit

options.label: D
options.text: A balanced budget

options.label: E
options.text: A $60 billion surplus

explanation: A surplus used to retire debt lowers the debt stock by the amount of the surplus. Reducing debt by $60 billion therefore requires a $60 billion annual surplus under the stated assumption.

prompt: Which of the following situations is internally consistent?

options.label: A
options.text: A government has a balanced current budget and therefore must have eliminated all national debt accumulated in prior years

options.label: B
options.text: A government has positive national debt and therefore cannot record a budget surplus in the current fiscal year

options.label: C
options.text: A government has a $25 billion budget surplus this year and still has $2 trillion in national debt

options.label: D
options.text: A government records a current budget surplus and therefore its accumulated national debt must become negative immediately

options.label: E
options.text: A government has a current budget deficit and therefore must have zero accumulated national debt at the end of the year

explanation: A current-year surplus and a positive national debt can coexist because the surplus is a flow and the debt is an accumulated stock. Past deficits can leave debt outstanding even when the current budget is positive.

prompt: A government has a $50 billion deficit this year, accumulated debt of $3 trillion, and rising required interest payments. Which statement best separates the three concepts?

options.label: A
options.text: The interest payment is the accumulated national debt, the $50 billion deficit measures total past borrowing, and the $3 trillion debt is annual government outlays

options.label: B
options.text: The $3 trillion debt is the current-year budget gap, the $50 billion deficit is the accumulated stock, and interest payments are counted as tax revenue

options.label: C
options.text: The deficit, national debt, and interest burden all measure the same fiscal condition, differing only in whether the amount is reported annually or cumulatively

options.label: D
options.text: The $50 billion deficit is accumulated past borrowing, the $3 trillion debt is the current-year shortfall, and rising interest payments reduce the debt stock

options.label: E
options.text: The $50 billion deficit is the current-year shortfall, the $3 trillion debt is accumulated past borrowing, and rising interest payments increase the opportunity cost of carrying that debt

explanation: The annual deficit is the current-year shortfall, while national debt is accumulated borrowing from past shortfalls. Interest payments are the carrying cost of that debt and create an opportunity cost by absorbing government funds.

prompt: A government moves from a $20 billion surplus to a $30 billion deficit. Assuming the surplus in the first year was used to retire debt, how does debt change across the two years relative to its initial level?

options.label: A
options.text: It returns exactly to its initial level

options.label: B
options.text: It ends $10 billion below its initial level

options.label: C
options.text: It ends $20 billion above its initial level

options.label: D
options.text: It ends $30 billion below its initial level

options.label: E
options.text: It ends $10 billion above its initial level

explanation: The first-year $20 billion surplus reduces debt by $20 billion, while the second-year $30 billion deficit adds $30 billion. The net two-year change is therefore +$10 billion.

prompt: A government collects $1.10 trillion in taxes, spends $850 billion on purchases, and pays $230 billion in transfers. In the following year, taxes rise by $20 billion, purchases rise by $15 billion, and transfers rise by $10 billion. Which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.text: A $20 billion surplus becomes a $5 billion deficit

options.label: B
options.text: A $20 billion surplus becomes a $15 billion surplus

options.label: C
options.text: A $20 billion deficit becomes a $15 billion deficit

options.label: D
options.text: A $20 billion deficit becomes a $25 billion deficit

options.label: E
options.text: A $20 billion surplus becomes a $25 billion surplus

explanation: Initial balance is 1.10 - (0.85 + 0.23) = +$0.02 trillion, or a $20 billion surplus. The next-year change is +20 - 15 - 10 = -$5 billion, so the surplus falls to $15 billion.
